-33.8393,151.20056: Henry Lawson lived and wrote of this district in No's 21, 26, 28, 30, 31 Euroka Street at various times from 1914 to 1921 previously in other north Sydney houses from 1892
-33.84174,151.2216: May Gibbs 1877-1969 Creator of Snugglepot, Cuddlepie, Banksia Men and Gunmut Babies. Lived, wrote and illustrated her books here
-33.85779,151.21494: Rudyard Kipling 1865-1936 Sydney ... was populated by leisured multitudes all in their shirt-sleeves and all picnicking all the day. They volunteered that they were new and young, but would do wonderful things some day. Something of Myself (1937) Rudyard Kipling visited Sydney in 1891. A prolific writer of verse and stories, including the two volumes of The Jungle Book, he had a strong influence on Australian poets like 'Banjo' Paterson.
-33.86986,151.21037: Former Supreme Court and Registry Office
-33.8748,151.21245: Sydney Grammar School. This building was completed in 1835 and occupied by the Sydney College until 1850. Since 1857 it has been occupied by Sydney Grammar School. The Inauguration of the University of Sydney took place here in 1852.
-33.87897,151.19977: Locomotive No.1 The oldest surviving steam locomotive in Australia Built by Robert Stephenson & Co. in 1854, this is the only locomotive designed by James McConnell, one of the founders of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, to have been preserved. Locomotive No.1 symbolises the transformation of social, industrial and commercial life in New South Wales through British railway technology.

Boulton and Watt Engine The oldest rotative steam engine in the world. Built in 1785, it powered Whitbread's London Brewary until 1887. James Watt demonstrated this engine to King George III when he visited the brewary in 1787. This engine marks the start of mass industrialisation and the exponential increase in our use of fossil fuel.
-33.88009,151.20839: The Tivoli Theatre. Opened as The Adelphi in 1911 and later known as the Grand Opera House, a theatre, renamed the New Tivoli in 1932, occupied this site until 1969. It was famous as the home of vaudeville in Sydney.
